attribution: Credited to the work the manuscript cites, not to OpenAI or the manuscript's authors. The manuscript says: “We use the classical dyadic decomposition of an AD-regular set; see [1, Section 4, p. 12] for its scale and finite-diameter conventions, and [4] for the construction.” Its bibliography: “[1] Jonas Azzam, Mihalis Mourgoglou, and Michele Villa, Quantitative differentiability on uni- formly rectifiable sets, 2025, arXiv:2306.13017v2, revised 13 November 2025; first posted 2023.” Its bibliography: “[4] , Analysis of and on uniformly rectifiable sets, Mathematical Surveys and Monographs, vol. 38, American Mathematical Society, Providence, RI, 1993.” Quoted from openai/math (Apache-2.0); AMVO has not consulted or checked the cited work.
scope: Proposition 1.8 (Regular dyadic cells) of the manuscript “Riesz transforms and uniform rectifiability in higher codimension” (preprints/Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiability-in-higher-codimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 081 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8445a9b1c8e5a4c3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: If DE > 0, there are a common µ-null set N ⊂ E and families Dk of Borel cells in E \ N such that: (i) each Dk partitions E \ N, and cells of different generations are disjoint or nested; (ii) writing ℓ(Q) = 2−k for Q ∈ Dk, there are centers zQ ∈ Q and constants 0 < c0 ≤ 1/2, C0 ≥ 2 for which (E \ N) ∩ B(zQ, c0ℓ(Q)) ⊂ Q ⊂ E ∩ B(zQ, C0ℓ(Q)), c1ℓ(Q)n ≤ µ(Q) ≤ C1ℓ(Q)n ; (iii) every non-top cell has one parent, and every cell has finitely many children. When DE = ∞, all integer generations are available. When DE < ∞, there is a largest scale ℓ0 with DE ≤ ℓ0 < 2DE, and finitely many cells at that scale. All constants depend only on d, n, CAD.
